title: Third round of US-Ukraine-Russia talks opens in Geneva
body:
On 17 February 2026, a new round of peace negotiations in a trilateral format between Ukraine, the United States and Russia began in Geneva, Switzerland. According to European Pravda, Switzerland organised the meeting and provided the conditions for the talks. The round followed earlier meetings in Abu Dhabi.

Rustem Umerov, Secretary of Ukraine's National Security and Defence Council, headed the Ukrainian delegation. He said the delegation was operating within a framework approved by President Volodymyr Zelensky and had a clear mandate. Umerov said the agenda included security and humanitarian issues and described the approach in these words: "We are working constructively, focused and without excessive expectations."

Euromaidan Press, citing Suspilne, reported that this was the third round of the trilateral talks, after rounds in Abu Dhabi on 23 and 24 January and on 4 and 5 February 2026, which produced no concrete agreements to halt the war. The Geneva talks were scheduled to conclude on 18 February. Representatives of the United Kingdom and France and an adviser to the German chancellor on foreign and security policy took part in a consultative capacity. The stated goal was to advance steps that could lead to a sustainable peace.
